Turyi Remety Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Turii Remety, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1854 per epigraphic data, used until WWII, with its latest preserved gravestone dating to 1942. Jews are believed to have arrived in the early 19th century; population reached 45 by 1830 and about 162 (12%) by 1880, rising to 235 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; from 1940-1941, area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Population reached 168 by 1941; some families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered. Some Jews were deported to Auschwitz in 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
